cd /home/nab-raj.roshyara@dg-nexolution.de/roshyara/personal/nrna1/docs/knowledgeos/knowlegeos_manual_theory_20261018/06-theory/manuscript; python3 -I - <<'EOF'
p='chapter_01/CH-01-knowledge-authority-execution.md'; s=open(p).read()
R=[
# R1-4 §1.16.1 check and effect
("This is §1.14.5 (gates follow ratification) for **modelling**: a model may not settle a question that is still open.",
 """This is §1.14.5 (gates follow ratification) for **modelling**: a model may not settle a question that is still open.

**Check and effect belong to one atomic change (Src: DE L342–352, L58; Ded).** A later source states the rule for message handling: "a check performed *before* an effect is not deduplication; it is a race". The general form: **a condition read at one instant and acted on at another, with nothing guaranteeing it still holds** [DE L352]. The same applies to **authority**. An authorization checked before an act and relied on after it may have ended in between. So the check and the effect it licenses must fall within one atomic change, or the check must be repeated at the effect. The same source adds that an event announcing a change may be published only **after** the change committed; otherwise it reports a state change that did not happen [DE L58]."""),
# R1-5 §1.16.4 event categories
("**The list omits the anchor:** the **record of the human act itself** and the **grant** under which it was made (§1.13).",
 """**The kinds of event, elaborated by a later source (Src, PROPOSED; DE L78–96).**

| Kind | What it is |
|---|---|
| **domain event** | an internal fact in the shared vocabulary |
| **notification** | an in-process dispatch mechanism, not a contract |
| **integration event** | crosses a boundary; a versioned, deliberately smaller published contract |
| **audit event** | an accountability record: actor, policy version, provenance |

"An audit event may be generated from a domain event but is not identical to it" [DE L91]. That is a report of an act, not the act (INV-A1), at the event layer. The source also rejects a single vague "knowledge updated" event: it carries no domain fact, so **every receiver must re-derive what happened**, which gives many independent interpretations of one fact [DE L15–37]. That is the one-owner principle (P-7) violated by construction.

**The list omits the anchor:** the **record of the human act itself** and the **grant** under which it was made (§1.13)."""),
# R1-6 §1.16.6 retention
("Supersession as a link (I-7) makes pinning cheap: old versions persist, so *d*@*v* stays resolvable.",
 """Supersession as a link (I-7) makes pinning cheap: old versions persist, so *d*@*v* stays resolvable.

**Retention follows from pinning (Ded; Src DE L398–408).** If a claim pins *d*@*v*, then *d*@*v* must stay resolvable for as long as the claim may be checked. In particular, a record whose deletion would make a recorded authority act unverifiable, such as the pinned version of the grant behind an exception, cannot be deleted. A later source draws the same conclusion for events: "retention for governance-critical events is bounded by **reconstructability**, not by operational convenience" [DE L406]. *Derivation:* reconstructability (premise R, Ch. 0 §0.5) plus pinning implies retention. **No time-to-live may apply to a pinned referent.**"""),
# R1-7 §1.16.8 approval reference provenance
("A present reference is evidence of a **claim** of authority, not of authority.",
 """A present reference is evidence of a **claim** of authority, not of authority.

**Where the reference came from also matters (Src: DE L113–131, L277–301; Ded).** A later source contrasts two activation designs:
- **from the caller:** the activation receives the approval reference from the caller (`activate(approval_reference)`). It **executes an approval already recorded**;
- **from the evaluator:** an evaluator **produces** the reference during the activating transaction.

"A mechanism that produces the approval reference has granted the authority that reference is supposed to record" [DE L295]. The presence check passes in both cases, so **it cannot detect the difference** [DE L297]. Hence a further condition (Ded): an authority reference must resolve to an act **recorded before, and independently of,** the transaction that relies on it. The source proposes this as a new invariant (its OQ-33)."""),
]
for a,b in R:
    assert s.count(a)==1,a[:50]; s=s.replace(a,b)
a="> - **DR**: `docs/knowledge_tranfer/20260816_1040_decision_register.md` (AI-generated, PROPOSED; a consolidation of 29 open questions)"
s=s.replace(a,a+"\n> - **DE**: `docs/knowledge_tranfer/20260816_1044_domain_events.md` (AI-generated, PROPOSED; with addenda on outbox and inbox; external citations unverified)")
open(p,'w').write(s); print('ok')
EOF
